features.text: Patient has a foot ulcer on the right foot that has been present for approximately six to eight weeks and has not been resolving.
Patient reports no pain in the affected foot.
Patient has a history of diabetes and is on insulin.
Patient's blood sugar levels have been running higher than normal, and the last hemoglobin A1c was above nine.
Patient believes the ulcer may have been caused by stepping on a nail or other trauma while working in the backyard.
Patient reports no fever or chills.
Patient experiences occasional numbness and tingling in the feet, especially in cold weather.
Patient has a history of smoking, having smoked for at least twenty years, with a rate of at least two packs per day, and quit approximately four years ago.
Patient does not experience calf pain when walking.
Patient is taking baby aspirin daily.
Patient does not have a podiatrist for yearly foot exams.
Patient has a history of tension headaches but no other significant symptoms such as chest pain or shortness of breath.
